extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators, graduate program designers, and middle-school mathematics teachers seeking professional development or graduate coursework
extracted.subtask_description: Design and deliver a graduate-level professional development program and courses for middle school mathematics teachers, including course sequencing, content selection (including discrete mathematics), pedagogy, assessment, and student supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: A master's program meant as professional development for certified teachers (not initial certification), to help them become highly qualified middle school mathematics teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on mathematics middle school teachers need; balance mathematics content and pedagogy; target practicing teachers who are already certified and employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure — content/pedagogy balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Half of the courses in the program are mathematics courses, and half are education courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure both strong mathematics content and pedagogy are represented so graduates are prepared to teach middle school math and meet local/state standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions requirements include a college degree with a 2.75 undergraduate GPA and current teaching certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to waive or substitute required courses for some students to meet varied backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course prerequisites and sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Many upper-level courses require MATH 505 (Discrete Mathematics) and current teaching certification; MATH 501/502 list prerequisites explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence courses (e.g., discrete math first) so teachers build a common foundation before exploring algebra, geometry, graph theory, number theory, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electives to tailor student needs
rubrics_metrics.description: After required mathematics and education courses, students may choose two electives from a listed set to tailor the program to their needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer electives (graph theory, number theory, operations research, special topics, independent study, action research, CS/IT courses) so students can shore up math background or pursue special interests (technology, projects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of curriculum materials aligned to teacher practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use textbooks from the Connecting Middle School and College Mathematics Project and NCTM Navigations Series that link teacher education to current middle school curricula and provide problems taken from middle school textbooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose materials that give teachers 'profound understanding of fundamental mathematics' and examples that can be used directly in classrooms; supplement with multiple curriculum examples and Praxis II materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical modeling and classroom practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Model best practices in teaching the courses by introducing activities and group work, using appropriate technology, having students research history of mathematics, and incorporating student projects and presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use class formats that mirror what teachers should use in their own classrooms (interactive, collaborative, technology-enhanced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology and labs
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate tools like The Geometer's Sketchpad (labs integral to courses) and computer lab visits as part of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guided discovery exercises and interactive files; explicitly teach teachers how to use such software with their students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course-specific content recommendations — discrete mathematics core areas
rubrics_metrics.description: NCTM-recommended discrete mathematics areas for K–12: combinatorics, iteration and recursion, and vertex-edge graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these areas in courses for prospective middle school teachers to prepare them to introduce discrete topics to students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph theory learning goals (K–8/middle grades recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should: represent situations with vertex-edge graphs and adjacency matrices; describe and apply properties of graphs (vertex degrees, edge weights, directed edges, isomorphism); use graphs to solve path/circuit/network problems including Euler paths, Hamilton paths, minimum spanning trees, and shortest paths; understand and apply vertex coloring to avoid conflicts; use algorithmic thinking and use graphs to solve optimization problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach explicit problem-solving and algorithmic approaches tied to real-world and abstract settings; align to grade-level progressions suggested in Navigation books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorics and iteration/recursion recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar grade-span recommendations exist for combinatorics and iteration/recursion (systematic counting; modeling sequential change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include activities and lessons that span recommended K–12 progressions so middle school teachers can introduce these ideas developmentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of algebra and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Use texts and activities that integrate algebraic and geometric ideas (e.g., Papick text integrates Pythagorean theorem with algebraic contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cross-topic examples that expand teachers' notions of what 'algebra' and 'geometry' are and show connections useful in middle-school curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and capstone considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently students are assessed at the individual course level, though a capstone experience (as used in high school track) could provide a more thorough framework for assessing the program as a whole and offer students reflection opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requiring a capstone project to integrate mathematical and pedagogical knowledge and to support program-level assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action research project expectations (EDUC 597)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of an action research special project: complete a thorough literature review, clarify a hypothesis about a classroom learning/teaching problem, collect baseline data, design and monitor an intervention, test the effect of the proposed solution, and reflect/generalize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action research spans two semesters and culminates in a presentation of findings; require instructor approval for topic and expect systematic data collection and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student support structures — TA and office hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide extensive instructor office hours and supplement with a teaching assistant (a recent successful student) who meets weekly with the instructor, leads optional problem sessions, and gives feedback on student difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a TA program (tuition waiver as compensation) to extend available help and provide peer-level support and diagnostic feedback to instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling practices and trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses are often taught once per week in a three-hour marathon because teachers cannot attend more frequently; although shorter blocks are preferred, classes can be broken into segments (lecture, activity, group work, computer lab) to mitigate fatigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design course meeting times mindful of teachers' schedules and travel burdens; structure sessions with varied activities to maintain engagement during long meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class size and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Small class sizes (around 20–25) are valued because they allow high participation and close interaction among classmates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain relatively small cohorts to promote discussion, collaboration, and individualized feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation and stakeholder feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seek feedback from students (surveys, anecdotal reports) and convene a program-level advisory council of teachers, administrators, community college faculty, and program participants to review student performance and program needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey data and advisory meetings to inform program changes (e.g., considering capstone) and to ensure the program meets district needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with state/national standards and assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Design courses to help teachers learn content related to state Core Learning Goals (e.g., Maryland Core Learning Goals for High School Algebra/Data Analysis and Geometry) and to prepare teachers to support students for state assessments such as the HSA and Praxis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly examine local, state, national, and international standards and assessments in pedagogy courses; use these standards to shape course content and instructional strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple curriculum sources for motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchase and use copies of school textbooks from NCTM-based curricula (Connected Mathematics, Discovering Mathematics) to motivate class activities and connect graduate-level topics to classroom materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage real classroom curriculum materials so teachers see direct applicability and can map graduate content to their own teaching resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special topics and flexible offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer rotating special topics (MATH 599) such as mathematical modeling, calculus-related explorations, or other themes relevant to middle school teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide summer offerings and rotating topics to broaden teachers' exposure and allow scheduling flexibility.
